headline: Cultural Commission Reviews Pāʻia Town Mixed-Use Development Project

meeting.body: Cultural Commission Reviews Pāʻia Town Mixed-Use Development Project
meeting.summary: The Cultural Resources Commission heard a consultation request for a Pāʻia mixed-use project with housing and parking; no one testified.
meeting.recap: The commission heard a consultation request on a cultural impact assessment for a proposed mixed-use project in Pāʻia town.[[0:00:00]] The vice chair said she works for the archaeology firm that sent the request, and she recused herself (stepped aside) from the item.[[0:00:35]] The commission could hear the presentation and ask questions but could not take an action that would count as commission comments.[[0:01:04]] No one testified.[[0:03:05]] A consultant for the firm said plans include public parking to ease parking problems in town.[[0:04:56]] Plans also include multifamily housing meant for affordable housing.[[0:05:07]] The firm asked for referrals to people or families who know the area's history and land use.[[0:06:46]] One commissioner offered to connect the firm with more families.[[0:10:09]] Another commissioner asked whether managed retreat (moving back from a shoreline that is falling into the ocean) was considered.[[0:12:05]] The consultant said that is a question for the developer, and the firm will ask it.[[0:13:42]] A commissioner asked about traffic, saying the area is already congested.[[0:16:15]] The consultant said the plan is to move the one-way mini bypass road and make it two-way.[[0:16:45]]
meeting.next: The firm will ask the project developer about managed retreat for people on the shoreline. The consultant said concerns heard about impacts to makai (ocean-side) resources will need to go into the report.

moments.q: Vice chair recuses herself from the item
Traffic plan: relocated two-way bypass road
